darkniche — package design

Source: DESIGN.md

Directional niche coverage, climatic dark diversity, and threshold-sweep null-model diagnostics. R port of the ddniche Python pipeline (v2.1) underlying Rahimi & Jung (Iran companion study, in review) and the global ecoregion study.

Design principles

  1. Data-agnostic core. The package ships no range polygons, no ecoregion shapefile, no rasters. Users bring point sets or cell scores in a shared environmental space; the package never downloads anything. IUCN polygons and the WWF shapefile are inputs to the user’s workflow, not package data (both are too large and licence-encumbered to bundle). The vignette demonstrates the full workflow, and the published results for 619 ecoregions are bundled via dn_data() so every example runs on real output.
  2. Numerical fidelity. Every core function reproduces the Python reference to float32 precision, enforced by golden tests generated from the actual ddniche code (tests/testthat/test-golden.R, tools/make_golden.py). Passing golden tests are the package’s correctness claim; any future refactor must keep them green.
  3. Guardrails are API, not prose. The two field-tested failure modes are encoded in the objects themselves: dn_aggregate() returns reliable = FALSE (and suppresses SES/enrichment) when the expected count is < 5, and dn_sweep() prints a direction-reversal warning when the verdict flips across thresholds. dn_cddr() computes the area-adjusted residual alongside the raw ratio and documents that raw CDDR must never be used to rank regions.
  4. Base R first. v0.1 has zero hard dependencies beyond base + stats. terra is Suggests-only (for users projecting rasters). An Rcpp backend for dn_density()/dn_metrics() is a v0.2 optimisation once the API is frozen — profiling shows the pure-R KDE handles the package’s intended per-study scale (102–104 objects) comfortably; the 21.7M-pair global run remains the Python pipeline’s job.

Key API decisions

  • dn_null_shift(targets=) accepts explicit target cells so a draw can be reproduced exactly (used by the golden tests; also lets users share seeds across languages). Default behaviour draws availability-weighted targets.
  • dn_dark(p_min = 0.177): the default is the externally calibrated Youden threshold of the source studies’ species-blocked, climate-only establishment model. It is documented as their calibration; users applying different metrics/models must recalibrate via dn_calibrate() on their own validation positives.
  • dn_sweep() returns a classed object so that printing it in a console or an Rmd cannot silently drop the reversal warning.
  • Array layout: densities are R x R matrices indexed [x, y] (Python’s first axis = x). Flat vectors inside the package are R column-major; the golden tests handle the C-order conversion explicitly and document it.

Deliberate exclusions (v0.1)

  • The GBM establishment model (sklearn in the pipeline): out of scope; the calibrated threshold is provided as a documented constant, and dn_calibrate() covers recalibration. A glm-based equivalent is a candidate for v0.2.
  • Tail-refined permutation p-values (utils.permutation_p refinement): dn_null_breadth()/dn_null_summary() return the floored empirical p only. SES, null mean and SD — the quantities the dark-diversity rule uses — are golden-tested; the refined p is not yet ported. TODO(v0.2).
  • The 3-D lattice (niche.PCSpaceND): sensitivity-analysis machinery, not core. TODO(v0.2) behind the same API (dn_space(ndim = 3)).
  • Figures: the package plots only the sweep; publication figures stay in user scripts.

Test strategy

  1. Golden tests (56 assertions): lattice construction, KDE vs scipy gaussian_filter (< 2e-7), envelopes and entry quantiles (exact), all twelve pair metrics (< 5e-6; float32 reference), shift null with injected targets (exact for q; < 2e-4 for auc, limited by the reference’s own float32 weight storage), SES flooring (exact), aggregate test incl. reliability flags (exact), breadth-matched null (< 1e-6), and the containment phenomenon of the papers’ Figure 1 (DNC_q ≈ 1, DNC_auc ≈ 0.9, D ≈ 0.08 on the engulfing-niche pair).
  2. Real-data reproduction (pre-release gate): run tools/export_golden_real.py against the actual pipeline store to dump ~20 species x 10 ecoregions of real densities and metrics, and confirm the R port reproduces published table values. This is the step that needs files from the authors’ machine (see below).

Development workflow

Rscript -e 'roxygen2::roxygenise()'          # regenerate man/ and NAMESPACE
R CMD INSTALL --no-docs .
Rscript -e 'testthat::test_dir("tests/testthat", package = "darkniche")'
R CMD build . && R CMD check darkniche_0.1.0.tar.gz
R CMD Rd2pdf --no-preview --force \
  --title="darkniche: Climatic Dark Diversity and Directional Niche Coverage in R -- Reference Manual" \
  -o manual/darkniche-manual.pdf .
Rscript analysis/01_simulation.R && Rscript analysis/02_ecoregions.R \
  && Rscript analysis/03_schematics.R

Defect log

Kept deliberately, because each was found by a test rather than by reading:

  1. dn_sweep() used unreliable thresholds in its verdict (fixed in 0.1.0 before release). The reversal detection, the printed ratio range and the plotted curve were computed over all finite ratios, including rows where dn_aggregate() had suppressed the effect size for an expected count below five — so the diagnostic could report exactly the numbers the test refuses to report. All three now use reliable rows only, and attr(x, "n_reliable") exposes the count. Regression test: “the sweep verdict never uses cells the test calls unreliable”.
  2. dn_auc() returned NaN for single-class labels (fixed in 0.1.0). A validation set with no negatives produced NaN silently, which in a scripted workflow propagates into a results table without any signal that something went wrong. dn_auc(), dn_delong() and dn_calibrate() now stop with a message naming the problem, and dn_auc() also checks that score and label have equal length. Regression test: “degenerate inputs fail loudly rather than returning nonsense”.
  3. dn_cddr() warned on a constant ratio. cor() emits a zero-standard-deviation warning when every region has the same ratio; confound_r is now NA in that case and the report and plot say “not estimable”.
  4. README verification snippet did not run as written (fixed post-release, in documentation only). Two problems, both found by a user pasting it into a fresh session rather than by any test: the metric example printed values from an unseeded draw, so the printed output never matched the comment; and it told the reader to run testthat::test_local(system.file(package = "darkniche")), which fails because R does not install a package’s tests unless INSTALL_opts = "--install-tests" is passed. Documentation examples that quote expected output must either be seeded or must not quote output.
  5. CFI_w cell-ordering. The Mahalanobis weight grid must be enumerated in the same order as the flattened density. R densities flatten column-major (x fastest, matching expand.grid); the Python fixtures are C-order (x slowest). The golden test builds its own grid for the fixture ordering and documents why.

Roadmap

  • v0.1 (this release): core verified against the reference implementation, bundled ecoregion data, two case studies, PDF manual, R CMD check clean.
  • Distribution: GitHub only, installed with remotes::install_github(). A pkgdown site is built and deployed to GitHub Pages by CI on every push to main. CRAN submission is deliberately not a goal: an existing CRAN package, DarkDiv (Carmona & Partel), estimates dark diversity from co-occurrence, and a near-name collision would confuse users of both.
  • v0.2: compiled backends for dn_density() and dn_metrics(); permutation-p refinement; three-dimensional space; GLM establishment helper; pkgdown content expansion (further articles).
  • Software paper: Methods in Ecology and Evolution (Applications). The R-versus-Python agreement doubles as an independent-reimplementation robustness statement citable in both empirical papers’ revisions.
